data.name: Taliah
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Taliah is derived from the Hebrew word 'tal', which means 'dew' or 'rain'. The suffix 'iah' is added, which means 'of God'. Thus, Taliah's full meaning is 'Dew of God'. In the Bible, Taliah is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 7:14.

in_hebrew.name: תליה
in_hebrew.meaning: השם תליה פירושו תפילה לאלוהים או השבעה לאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם תליה הוא שם עברי שפירושו 'תפילה לאלוהים' או 'השבעה לאל'. הוא מורכב מהמילים 'תל' ו-'יה', שפירושם 'לעלות' ו-'אלוהים'. השם תליה מופיע בתנ"ך ככינויה של אחת הנשים המוזכרות בשושנת המלכים.

in_greek.name: Τάλια
in_greek.meaning: Το όνομα Τάλια σημαίνει προσευχή στο Θεό ή όμηση στο Θεό
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Τάλια είναι ελληνικό όνομα που σημαίνει 'προσευχή στο Θεό' ή 'όμηση στο Θεό'. Η ετυμολογία του ονόματος Τάλια συνδέεται με τις εβραϊκές λέξεις 'תל' και 'יה', που σημαίνουν 'να ανεβαίνει' και 'Θεός' αντίστοιχα.

historical_references.reference: Talia, a heroine in the early Christian apocryphal literature, is the wife of Zacharias, the father of John the Baptist. The story of Talia and Zacharias appears in the 'Gospel of the Nativity of John' and the 'Protevangelium of James'. In these texts, Talia is described as a barren woman who is miraculously healed by an angel when she is carrying John the Baptist. The time period for the composition of these texts is believed to be around the 2nd century AD.

historical_references.reference: Talia, a Christian martyr, is mentioned in the 'Martyrologium Hieronymianum' as having been a virgin and a deaconess in Bithynia. She was martyred during the reign of Emperor Maximian (286-305 AD) for refusing to offer sacrifices to the Roman gods. Her feast day is celebrated on November 22. In later legends, she was said to have been tortured and killed by having her limbs torn apart and then beheaded.
